# A rejected reveal round trip skips the Portal's theme switch entirely

## Context

Found by @neo-opus-grace reviewing PR #18127, which added a second caller of `startViewTransition()`. She flagged the awaited round trip as a new failure surface; it turned out to be a property of the **pattern**, present in the Portal since the reveal shipped. #18127 guards its own caller and deliberately did not widen into this one.

**Live latest-open sweep:** checked the latest 12 open issues at 2026-09-02T17:10Z; no equivalent found. **Confirmed at the source rather than assumed:** `ViewportController.mjs:285-291` has no `.catch()` on the await.

## The Problem

`Portal.view.ViewportController#onSwitchTheme` awaits a **remote** method and then applies the theme:

```js
await Neo.main.DomAccess.startViewTransition({...});

me.setTheme(newTheme)
```

The engine method itself is well behaved — it returns `false` without the View Transition API, and catches a rejected `ready` or a throwing registration internally, so it resolves rather than rejects. But `Neo.main.DomAccess.startViewTransition` **called from the App worker is a proxy**: it posts a message and returns a promise created worker-side. If that round trip rejects — for any reason the main-thread method never observes — the `await` throws, `setTheme` is never reached, and **the theme button silently does nothing**.

That is strictly worse than the outcome the call exists to improve. The reveal is decorative; losing it should cost an animation, not the feature.

## The Architectural Reality

The guard cannot live in the engine, and I checked before proposing it there. `DomAccess.startViewTransition` runs on the main thread and cannot see a transport failure of the promise the *worker* is holding — by the time the transport fails there is nothing for the callee to catch. Absorbing it in the remote-method bridge would silently swallow rejections for every remote call, which is far too broad. So the guard belongs at each caller that treats the result as decorative.

| caller | file:line | state |
|---|---|---|
| Workstation | `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` | guarded in PR #18127, with a red-first arm |
| Portal | `apps/portal/view/ViewportController.mjs:285` | **unguarded — this ticket** |

## The Fix

Append `.catch(() => {})` to the awaited call in `onSwitchTheme`, and state in a comment why a decorative call must not be able to take the theme change down with it. Mirror #18127's unit arm: a stub that rejects, asserting the theme still flips and nothing throws — the arm must fail without the guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a rejected `startViewTransition` round trip still applies the Portal's theme switch, with no throw.
- [ ] **AC-2** — the arm is red without the guard and green with it, and no other arm changes state under that mutation.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the existing behaviour is untouched when the call resolves: the reveal still plays and the flip still lands inside the `delay` window.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the comment explains the transport-vs-callee distinction, since the engine method looks infallible from the call site and that appearance is exactly what makes the omission easy.

## Out of Scope

- **Any change to `DomAccess` or the remote-method bridge.** Explained above: the callee cannot see this, and a bridge-level catch would swallow rejections for every remote call in the framework.
- **Auditing every other awaited remote call for the same shape.** Worth doing as its own sweep with its own evidence; bundling it here would turn a two-line fix into an open-ended audit.

## Avoided Traps

- **Pushing the guard into the engine because two callers need it.** The "N sites, one idiom" instinct is usually right and is wrong here — the engine is on the far side of the boundary that fails.
- **Fixing this inside PR #18127.** The Portal's defect is true whether or not that PR exists, so it is not required for it; folding it in would have made an approved diff grow past its stated scope.

## Related

- PR #18127 / #18125 — the Workstation caller, guarded, where this was found.
- #17739 / PR #17743 — the engine contract that documents what `startViewTransition` can and cannot observe.
